finding.claim: Missing authorization enforcement in update_doc: can_edit() result is discarded, so any user who can reach the endpoint can overwrite any document body. The sibling endpoint correctly uses require_edit().
finding.source: Any authenticated (or any request-bearing) user sending PUT /doc/<doc_id> with JSON {"body": ...}; doc_id is attacker-chosen
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] at docs.py:20 (write to the document store)

trace.note: doc = DOCS[doc_id] fetched without any ownership check
can_edit(g.user, doc) called but return value ignored, so no abort(403)

finding.guards_checked: can_edit is evaluated but unenforced (no if/abort). require_edit, used in update_title at line 27, is not called here. No auth decorator or before_request hook is visible in the file; g.user origin is not defined here.

verdict.guard_found: none effective: can_edit (docs.py:7) returns a bool but is a bare statement at docs.py:19; require_edit (docs.py:11-13) aborts but is only used at line 27. No before_request or auth decorator exists in the file.
verdict.reason: docs.py:19 calls can_edit() and discards the bool, so docs.py:20 overwrites doc["body"] for any caller who can reach PUT /doc/<doc_id> (a low-privilege non-editor user included), while the sibling at docs.py:27 correctly uses the aborting require_edit().

verdict_facts.guard_found: none effective: can_edit (docs.py:7) returns a bool and is called as a bare statement at line 19; no decorator or before_request hook exists in the directory
